summary: Cross-agent protocol consistency review of translator / fuzzer / cutover-gate
prompt: You are reviewing the three StranglerRoom Switch room agents together: agents/translator_agent.py (@translator), agents/fuzzer_agent.py (@fuzzer) and agents/cutover_agent.py (@cutover-gate), built on agents/runtime.py (RoomAgent: dispatch, say, handoff, ask_human, classify), agents/commands.py (the shared command grammar, handoff builders and MARK message prefixes) and agents/ledger.py (the three single-writer room documents and their state blocks), against the binding contract docs/AGENTS_SPEC.md (sections 1-2). The individual agents were already reviewed in isolation; this review is about the CROSS-AGENT PROTOCOL: the whole loop human 'migrate' -> translator v1 + handoff 'shadow-test' -> fuzzer campaign + human decision request -> human 'preserve D-1 D-2 D-4 and deprecate D-3 D-5' -> translator v2 + 're-verify' handoff -> fuzzer approved parity + 'benchmark' handoff -> cutover-gate card + approval request -> human 'approve-cutover' -> proxy flip + 'record-cutover' handoff -> translator seals the ledger. Produce ONE file, .hacp/reviews/agents_protocol.md, containing a section headed exactly '## Findings' with a numbered list of CONCRETE defects only, each with: file:line reference(s), severity (high/medium/low), a concrete failing scenario (room messages / document state -> wrong behaviour), and the fix. Look especially for: (1) wire-format drift: a field one agent writes into its document state (matrix runs/trigger/migration/report.clusters/registry; scorecard benchmarks[].rev/migration/legacy.p99_ms, cutover.proxy_target/approved_by/approval_message_id/rev/migration; ledger migration.id/builds[].rev/decisions[id].decision/by/tag) under a different name, shape or type than the reader in another agent expects; (2) handoff bodies built with agents/commands.py builders that the receiver's parse_* function would parse differently (rev/migration regexes, the decisions tail of re-verify, verb-first rule); (3) rev or migration-id mismatches between what the translator deploys/records, what the fuzzer verifies and records, what the cutover-gate benchmarks/flips and what record-cutover checks (case, length, which build is 'latest'); (4) trust checks: each reader verifies the document creator (created_by_agent_id vs RoomInfo.agents) and the sender (human vs specific agent) consistently - find any path where a compromised agent or a same-named document could drive another agent, and any human-only command (migrate, preserve/deprecate, approve-cutover, rollback) that an agent could trigger; governance refusals must start with MARK['governance_refusal']; (5) mention hygiene: any posted text (say/ask_human/error paths/status) in which an '@name' of an AGENT appears outside the deliberate handoff, including echoing room text or document fields without defusing; ask_human bodies must not contain '@translator' / '@cutover-gate'; (6) MARK prefixes: every message the e2e driver waits for must START with the MARK text (after the '@target ' Switch adds on send_targeted); (7) idempotency / redelivery across agents (a re-delivered handoff or a repeated approve-cutover must not double-seal, double-flip or loop between agents); (8) ping-pong risk: any agent replying to another agent's non-command message with a message that addresses that agent. Do not report style nits or things that are fine. After '## Findings' you may add '## Notes' for non-defect observations.
